# Use Case

## Background

It is hard to talk about the history of the **Philadelphia Chinatown** without the construction of **I-676**, also known as the **Vine Street Expressway**. Although the highway serves as a significant thoroughfare through Center City Philadelphia, the indispensable repercussion on the adjacent neighborhoods still lingers today. Consequences of the highway such as demolishment of buildings, pedestrian safety threats, traffic congestion, as well as noise and air pollutions had been harming Chinatown and its surrounding neighborhoods over the past decades and are yet to be addressed.

Standing in opposition to the issues, [City of Philadelphia Office of Transportation and Infrastructure and Sustainability (OTIS)](https://www.phila.gov/departments/office-of-transportation-and-infrastructure-systems/) brought forth the plan of capping sections of the expressway as a solution to address its historical harms on the Chinatown region. This “cap”, named **the Chinatown Stitch project**, aimed to create a safe and equitable green space for the public that would reconnect areas north and south to the Vine Street expressway. Receiving funds from the US department of Transportation and the local organizations, the construction of the Chinatown Stitch will start in 2027 and is expected to be completed in early 2030.

This purpose of this study is to help OTIS **understand the housing market of Philadelphia Chinatown region before and after the implementation of the Chinatown Stitch**. The first part of the study will focus the effects of highways on sales prices in the study region as well as the entire Philadelphia. House prices will then be estimated using **three predictive models under three different future scenarios**: business as usual without the implementation of the Chinatown Stitch, business as usual with the implementation of the Chinatown Stitch, and an alternative future in which the Chinatown Stitch significantly reshapes the urban landscape of the study region.

![](Final%20R%20Markdown/Images/background.png)

Three study areas are used in the analysis to reveal the effects of I-676 on the land market of the Chinatown region.

-   **Referable study area (Philadelphia):** to analyse the impact of different highways on the surrounding land markets in the context of the city.
-   **Main study area (10 block groups):** to figure out the correlation between I-676 and property sales price and make future predictions based on three potential scenarios.
-   **Compared study area (north and south sides):** to investigate the different situations of the Chinatown region under the construction of I-676.

```{r StudyArea_plot}
StudyArea_plot1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = Philly_blockgroup, fill = "transparent", color = "grey90", linewidth = .2) +
  geom_sf(data = studyarea, fill = "#eb5600", color = "#eb5600") +
  geom_sf(data = hydro, fill = "#DFF3E3", color = "transparent") +
  geom_sf(data = philly_bounds, fill = "transparent", color = "grey60", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Three Study Areas:",
       subtitle = "Philadelphia | 10 Block Groups around the Chinatown Stitch | North and South Sides",
       caption = "Source: ACS Census Data and OPA Data.") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold",margin = margin(b = 6)),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 10)),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 10)))

  geom_sf(data = studyarea_north, fill = alpha("#eb5600", .1), color = "transparent") +
  geom_sf(data = studyarea_south, fill = alpha("#1a9988", .1), color = "transparent") +

  geom_sf(data = property_north, color = "#eb5600", size = .6) +
  geom_sf(data = property_south, color = "#1a9988", size = .6) +
  geom_sf(data = studyarea, fill = "transparent", color = "grey60", linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_void()
```

In the vision of **a city park** in the future, the Chinatown Stitch will bring vitality to local residents and visitors along with other green spaces. Connected with the Stitch, the **Rail Park** in the [north (Callowhill neighborhood)]{style="color: #eb5600;"} is still in construction and will make an impact years later. With a foundation of **cultural and commercial resources**, the [southern part (Chinatown neighborhood)]{style="color: #1a9988;"} will provide services to the surrounding area, including the city center of Philadelphia.

```{r UseCase_plot}
UseCase <- leaflet() %>%

              color = "grey",
              weight = 0.8,
              fillColor = "#DFF3E3",

  addPolygons(data = Chinatown_Callowhill,
              color = "#eb5600",
              weight = 1,
              opacity = 0.5,
              dashArray = "5,5",
              fillColor = "#eb5600",
              fillOpacity = 0.1) %>%
  addPolygons(data = park_4326,
              color = "#1a9988",
              weight = 1,
              fillOpacity = 0.6,
              fillColor = "#1a9988") %>%
  addPolygons(data = landuse_park_ing,
              color = "#1a9988",
              weight = 2,
              opacity = 0.8,
              fill = FALSE) %>%
  addPolylines(data = I676_4326,
               color = "#eb5600",
               opacity = 1,
               weight = 2) %>%
  addPolygons(data = ChinatownStitch_4326,
              color = "#eb5600",
              weight = 2,
              opacity = 1,
              fillColor = "#1a9988",
              fillOpacity = 0.8
              # fill = alpha("#1a9988", 0.5)
              ) %>%
  fitBounds(
    lng1 = bbox$xmin, 
    lat1 = bbox$ymin, 
    lng2 = bbox$xmax, 
    lat2 = bbox$ymax
  )

div(class = "center-leaflet", UseCase)
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet = TRUE, results='hide'}
)

# Property1_property2_census_join

  mutate(census_tract = as.numeric(census_tract))
tract_studyarea_selected <- tract_studyarea %>%
  select(GEOID_trimmed, TotalPoverty, MaleBachelors, FemaleBachelors, TotalPop) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

property1_geometry <- st_geometry(property1)

tract_studyarea_selected <- tract_studyarea_selected %>%
  distinct(GEOID_trimmed, .keep_all = TRUE)
property1 <- property1_blockgroup %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%

  mutate(objectid = as.character(objectid))
```

```{r Sijia POI, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results='hide', eval = FALSE}
# POI - restaurant-drink-dessert
api_key <- "AIzaSyCa-yuy1Y3n07URlR2HHg6dp_cIEouv9hs"
keywords <- c("restaurant", "dim sum restaurant", "kitchen", "desert","tea", "bubble tea","matcha", "herbal tea")
place_types <- c("restaurant", "cafe", "bakery")

studyarea_proj <- st_transform(block2023_studyarea, 2272)

grid_pts <- st_make_grid(studyarea_proj, cellsize = 2000, what = "centers")
grid_pts <- st_sf(geometry = grid_pts) %>%
  st_filter(st_buffer(studyarea_proj, 1000)) 

grid_pts_wgs <- st_transform(grid_pts, 4326)
coords <- st_coordinates(grid_pts_wgs)

all_responses <- list()

for (pt_idx in seq_len(nrow(coords))) {
  location <- coords[pt_idx, c(2,1)]  # lat, lng
  cat(" Querying center point", pt_idx, "at", paste(location, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  
  for (ptype in place_types) {
    for (kw in keywords) {
      Sys.sleep(5)  
      cat("🔎", kw, "in", ptype, "\n")

      response <- google_places(
        keyword = kw,
        location = location,
        radius = 2000,  
        place_type = ptype,
        key = api_key
      )

      if (is.null(response[["results"]]) || length(response[["results"]]) == 0) {
        cat("No results for:", kw, "in", ptype, "\n")
        next
      }

      page_token <- response$next_page_token
      results_list <- list(response[["results"]])
      i <- 1

      while (!is.null(page_token)) {
        Sys.sleep(10)
        response_next <- google_places(
          keyword = kw,
          location = location,
          radius = 2000,
          place_type = ptype,
          key = api_key,
          page_token = page_token
        )

        if (is.null(response_next[["results"]]) || length(response_next[["results"]]) == 0) break

        results_list[[i + 1]] <- response_next[["results"]]
        page_token <- response_next$next_page_token
        i <- i + 1
      }

      all_responses[[paste(kw, ptype, pt_idx, sep = "_")]] <- bind_rows(results_list) %>%
        filter(!is.na(place_id)) %>%
        distinct(place_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
    }
  }
}

clean_property_poi_distances <- function(property_sf) {
  property_sf %>%
    mutate(
      nearest_grocery_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_grocery_dist),
      nearest_restaurant_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_restaurant_dist)) %>%
    select(
      -nearest_grocery_dist,
      -nearest_restaurant_dist
    )
}
```

```{r neighborhood_process}
calculate_nearest_distance <- function(set_points, other_layer) {
  nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(set_points, other_layer)
  st_distance(set_points, other_layer[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()
```

## Philadelphia Scale Analysis

Before jumping into modeling, we first explored the relationship between **distance to highway** and **property prices**. We used property data from OPA Philadelphia that was cleaned to include only the data from the last five years (Jan. 1st, 2020 to Dec. 31st, 2024) with prices adjusted for inflation after removing extreme outliers and improbable values (keeping rows with property price within the 5th and 95th percentile), and keeping properties with total area of over 100 square feet (see map below for the properties included in this analysis).

Our **Philadelphia Scale Analysis** looks at properties (of all kinds, not limited to housing properties) within 500 m of Philadelphia's main highways -- [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"} on the East, [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"} on the West, [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"} in the North, and [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} through the city. We saw the following trends in property prices.


```{r prop500_med_saleprices}
  pull(count)

prop_count_us1 <- prop_count %>% 
  filter(grepl("US", closest_highway)) %>% 
  pull(count)

prop_count_i76 <- prop_count %>% 
  filter(grepl("-76", closest_highway)) %>% 
  pull(count)

prop_count_i95 <- prop_count %>% 
  filter(grepl("95", closest_highway)) %>% 
  pull(count)
```

`r paste0(substr(nrow(prop500), 1, 2), ",", substr(nrow(prop500), 3, 5))` total properties were included in this analysis. We see that the distribution of log sale prices of properties within 500m of highways in Philadelphia generally follow a normal distribution.

Though there aren't as many properties near [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} (`r prop_count_676` properties) as there are near the other highways, they are most expensive group with a median property price of **`r paste0('$', substr(med_price_676, 1, 3), ',', substr(med_price_676, 4, 9))`**. 

Properties near [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"} and [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"} are among a similar range of prices with median property prices being **`r paste0('$', substr(med_price_i95, 1, 3), ',', substr(med_price_i95, 4, 9))`** and **`r paste0('$', substr(med_price_i76, 1, 3), ',', substr(med_price_i76, 4, 9))`**, respectively, though there are almost five times as many properties near [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"} compared to [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"} (`r paste0(substr(prop_count_i95,1,1), ",", substr(prop_count_i95, 2,4))` and `r paste0(substr(prop_count_i76,1,1), ",", substr(prop_count_i76, 2,4))` properties around [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"} and [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, respectively). 

Finally, there are many properties within 500m of [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"} (`r paste0(substr(prop_count_us1,1,1), ",", substr(prop_count_us1, 2,4))` properties), but the median property price was lowest compared to other highways at **`r paste0('$', substr(med_price_us1, 1, 3), ',', substr(med_price_us1, 4, 9))`**.

```{r prop500_scatter}
scatter_4highways

```

The scatter plot above shows the relationship between distance to highway and property price along with the regression coefficients for each highway. We observe that without controlling for anything else, property prices generally increase (albeit by very little) as we move away from a highway which tracks with our literature review of highway effects on property prices. 

When predicting property price, the beta coefficient for log distance to highway is `r coef_i676`, `r coef_i76`, and `r coef_us1` for [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, and [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, respectively (note that the though the beta coefficients were significant with p < 0.01 for [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"} and [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, it was not statistically significant for [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} with a p = 0.069). 

For every 1% increase in distance from [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i676 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_i676)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** (assuming a block is about 200m). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i76 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_i76)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** if it were a block further from the highway. For every 1% increase in distance from [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_us1 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_us1)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** if it were a block further from the highway.

The exception here is for properties within 500m of [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, where the beta coefficient for log distance to highway is `r coef_i95` (p < 0.001). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, property price decreases by `r paste0(round(abs(1.01^coef_i95 - 1), 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", 100000 - round((4^coef_i95), 5)*100000)` less expensive**. We suspect that the negative effect distance to highways have on property price is driven by .....

We now zoom into our **study area** to further understand highway effects in our region of interest.

### same interpretation but with 100m instead of 200m

For every 1% increase in distance from [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i676 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", round((2^coef_i676)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** (assuming a block is about 100m). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i76 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((2^coef_i76)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** if it were a block further from the highway. For every 1% increase in distance from [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_us1 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((2^coef_us1)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** if it were a block further from the highway.

The exception here is for properties within 500m of [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, where the beta coefficient for log distance to highway is `r coef_i95` (p < 0.001). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, property price decreases by `r paste0(round(abs(1.01^coef_i95 - 1), 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", 100000 - round((2^coef_i95), 5)*100000)` less expensive**.


### Interpreting Philly Highway Effects (using median price of \$350,000 as base line and comparing to a property 200m further away from highway)

For every 1% increase in distance from [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i676 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$350,000 (median price of properties within 45-55m away from any Philly highway) is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block (assuming a block is about 200m) further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_i676)*350000) - 350000)` more expensive** (or a `r round(100*((4^coef_i676)*350000 - 350000)/350000, 1)` % change). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-76]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_i76 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_i76)*350000) - 350000)` more expensive** (`r round(100*((4^coef_i76)*350000 - 350000)/350000, 1)` % change) if it were a block further from the highway. For every 1% increase in distance from [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_us1 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_us1)*350000) - 350000)` more expensive** (`r round(100*((4^coef_us1)*350000 - 350000)/350000, 1)` % change) if it were a block further from the highway.

The exception here is for properties within 500m of [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, where the beta coefficient for log distance to highway is `r coef_i95` (p < 0.001). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, property price decreases by `r paste0(round(abs(1.01^coef_i95 - 1), 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", 350000 - round((4^coef_i95), 5)*350000)` less expensive** (`r round(100*((4^coef_i95)*350000 - 350000)/350000, 1)` % change).

### using Sijia's interpretation method
```{r prop500_predtable}
# models
lm_us1 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_to_closest_highway,
             data = prop500 %>% 
               filter(grepl("US", closest_highway)))

lm_i76 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_to_closest_highway,
             data = prop500 %>% 
               filter(grepl("-76", closest_highway)))

lm_i95 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_to_closest_highway,
             data = prop500 %>% 
               filter(grepl("95", closest_highway)))

lm_676 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_to_closest_highway,
             data = prop500 %>% 
               filter(grepl("676", closest_highway)))

distances <- seq(50, 250, by = 50)

# model predictions
pred_us1 <- exp(predict(lm_us1, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_to_closest_highway = log(distances))))

pred_i76 <- exp(predict(lm_i76, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_to_closest_highway = log(distances))))

pred_i95 <- exp(predict(lm_i95, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_to_closest_highway = log(distances))))

pred_676 <- exp(predict(lm_676, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_to_closest_highway = log(distances))))

# get predicted price changes from philly scale analysis
prop500_pred_table <- data.frame(
  Analysis_Scale = "Philadelphia",
  Distance_m = distances,
  US1_Prices = round(pred_us1),
  I76_Prices = round(pred_i76),
  I95_Prices = round(pred_i95),
  I676_Prices = round(pred_676),
  Chng_US1_Prices = round(pred_us1 - pred_us1[1]),
  Chng_I76_Prices = round(pred_i76 - pred_i76[1]),
  Chng_I95_Prices = round(pred_i95 - pred_i95[1]),
  Chng_I676_Prices = round(pred_676 - pred_676[1]),
  PercChng_US1_Prices = round(100*(pred_us1 - pred_us1[1])/pred_us1[1], 1),
  PercChng_I76_Prices = round(100*(pred_i76 - pred_i76[1])/pred_i76[1], 1),
  PercChng_I95_Prices = round(100*(pred_i95 - pred_i95[1])/pred_i95[1], 1),
  PercChng_I676_Prices = round(100*(pred_676 - pred_676[1])/pred_676[1], 1)
)
prop500_pred_table %>% 
  kbl(align = "c",
      caption = "Regression Predictions: Log Price ~ Log Distance to Closest Highway",
      col.names = c("Analysis Scale", "Distance (m)", "US-1 Prices", "I-76 Prices", "I-95 Prices", "I-676 Prices", "Change US-1 Prices", "Change I-76 Prices", "Change I-95 Prices", "Change I-676 Prices", "% Change US-1 Prices", "% Change I-76 Prices", "% Change I-95 Prices", "% Change I-676 Prices")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  row_spec(c(1,3), bold = T, background = "#7fe3d6")

```

For every 1% increase in distance from [US-1]{style="color: #1a9988;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^coef_res_us1 - 1, 4)*100,"%")`, meaning a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway would be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^coef_res_us1)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** if it were a block further from the highway.

The exception here is for properties within 500m of [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, where the beta coefficient for log distance to highway is `r coef_res_i95` (p < 0.001). For every 1% increase in distance from [I-95]{style="color: #eba075;"}, property price decreases by `r paste0(round(abs(1.01^coef_res_i95 - 1), 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", 100000 - round((4^coef_res_i95), 5)*100000)` less expensive**.

We now zoom into our **study area** to further understand highway effects in our region of interest.

### I-676 Effects

One of OTIS's key interests is the effect of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} on property prices nearby.  Here, we construct a relatively **simple linear model** with a few key predictors to look at the effect of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} on property prices while accounting for some control variables such as the square footage of the property, number of bathrooms, year built, zoning, and zip code among others.

For these analyses, we look at properties **within our study area**.

```{r i676effects_setup_studyareanew, quiet = TRUE, results = 'hide'}
# working with the newest philly_properties dataset where data was cleaned for our studyarea
property_studyarea_new <- st_read("Dataset/property_CT_FE.geojson") #1528 rows

# add features for simple linear regression
props_i676_tomodel <- property_studyarea_new %>% 
  # filter() %>% # there are a couple properties with total area < 100; reduces dataset to 990 properties
  # some feature engineering
  mutate(residential = ifelse(category_code_description %in% c("APARTMENTS  > 4 UNITS",
                                                               "MIXED USE",
                                                               "MULTI FAMILY",
                                                               "SINGLE FAMILY",
                                                               "GARAGE - RESIDENTIAL"),
                              1, 0), # is this property residential? (including mixed)
         
         building_code_description_new = case_when(
           grepl("FITNESS CENTER|GOV'T MUNICIPAL/STATE/FEDERAL", building_code_description_new) ~ "MostExpensive",
           grepl("LIFE CARE FACILITY-ASSTD LVNG|CORRECTIONAL|MEDICAL OFFICE BLDNG|PARKING GARAGE/DECK|BOARDING/ROOMING HOSUE|MIXED - RES/COMM|SCHOOL|BANK|OFFICE BLDNG - Mid Rise|DET MIXED-COM/RES-BLT AS COM", building_code_description_new) ~ "MoreExpensive",
           grepl("RETAIL - * SINGLE OCCUPANCY|ROW MIXED-COM/RES-BLT AS COM|ROW MODERN|APARTMENTS - LOW RISE|HOTEL - HI RISE|OFFICE BLDNG - Low Rise|FUNERAL HOME|RESTAURANT|DOWNTOWN ROW TYPE-* SNGL OCCP|WAREHOUSE|TWIN CONTEMPORARY|CAR WASH - AUTOMATIC|RETAIL CONDO|MANUFACTURING/PROCESSING|LOFT (INDUSTRIAL)|APARTMENTS - MID RISE|RELIGIOUS", building_code_description_new) ~ "Average",
           .default = "LeastExpensive" 
           ),
         building_code_description_new = factor(building_code_description_new),
      
         # all the other variables have been cleaned and feature engineered
) %>% 
  select(   # only keep vars necessary for model
    adj_sale_price,
    log_price, distance_to_I676, log_dist_highway,
    residential, 
    year_built, year_built_group,
    central_air, garage_spaces,
    number_of_bathrooms, number_of_bedrooms, total_area,
    exterior_condition, interior_condition, quality_grade,
    building_code_description_new, zoning_group,
    zip_code,
    I676_NS
  )

med_price_50m_studyarea <- props_i676_tomodel %>% 
  mutate(dist_to_i676m = distance_to_I676 * 0.3048) %>% 
  filter(dist_to_i676m > 45,
         dist_to_i676m < 55) %>% 
  pull(adj_sale_price) %>% 
  median() # 639764.6

```

```{r RMSE_calculator}
getRMSE <- function(model_results) {
  # residual sum of squares
  rss <- c(crossprod(model_results$residuals))
  # Mean squared error:
  mse <- rss / length(model_results$residuals)
  # Root MSE:
  RMSE <- sqrt(mse)
  
  return(RMSE)
}

```

#### Model Results

```{r i676effects_plot_studyareanew}
# model with just distance to highway
model_i676 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_highway,
                 data = props_i676_tomodel)
# log_dist_highway  0.11110
# Multiple R-squared:  0.01228,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.01163

model_i676_summary <- summary(model_i676)
model_i676_RMSE <- getRMSE(model_i676)

# scatter plot of dist to I-676 and property price
model_i676_scatter <- 
  ggplot(data = props_i676_tomodel, 
       aes(x = log_dist_highway, y = log_price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .2, size = 0.3, show.legend = F,
             color = "#7fe3d6") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", size = 1.2, show.legend = F,
              color = "#7fe3d6", fill = "#7fe3d6") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste(model_i676_table$Estimate[2]),
                x = 5.25,
                y = 14.25),
            color = "#7fe3d6",
            show.legend = F) +
  labs(title = "Property Price (log) as a function of Distance to I-676 (log)",
       subtitle = "Properties in Study Area",
       x = "Log Distance to I-676",
       y = "Log Property Price") +
  theme_minimal()

model_i676_scatter

```

```{r i676effects_model1_studyareanew}
# model with just distance to highway
model_i676 <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_highway,
                 data = props_i676_tomodel)
# log_dist_highway  0.11110
# Multiple R-squared:  0.01228,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.01163

model_i676_summary <- summary(model_i676)
model_i676_RMSE <- getRMSE(model_i676)

# create a clean table to show model results
model_i676_table <- data.frame(model_i676_summary$coefficients) %>% 
  rename(p = `Pr...t..`) %>% 
  select(Estimate, p) %>% 
  mutate(Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
         p = round(p, 3))
row.names(model_i676_table) <- c("Intercept", "Log Dist. to I-676")

model_i676_table %>% 
  kbl(align = c("l", rep("c", 2)),
      caption = "Regression Results: Log Price ~ Log Distance to I-676",
      col.names = c("Estimate", "p value")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  row_spec(2, bold = T, background = "#7fe3d6") %>% 
  add_footnote(label = paste0("R-squared: ", round(model_i676_summary$r.squared, 3), ", RMSE: ", round(model_i676_RMSE, 3)),
               notation = "none")

```

From an overly simple model, just looking at how logged distance to [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} predicts logged property price, we see that for properties within 500m of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, distance from the highway does not have a large effect on property price. We see that for every 1% increase in distance to the highway, **property price increases by `r paste0(round(1.01^model_i676_table$Estimate[2] - 1, 4)*100,"%")`**. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$650,000 (median price of properties between 45-55m from I-676) is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway (assuming a block is about 200m) to be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^model_i676_table$Estimate[2])*650000) - 650000)` more expensive** (`r round(100*((4^model_i676_table$Estimate[2])*650000 - 650000)/650000, 1)` % change). The R-squared value of the model is very low at `r round(model_i676_summary$r.squared, 3)` and the RMSE is very high `r round(model_i676_RMSE,3)`, meaning the model is terrible.

```{r i676effects_model2_studyareanew}
# simple model but with more predictors
model_i676_more <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_highway + 
                        residential + building_code_description_new + zoning_group + # internal characteristics
                        year_built_group + central_air + 
                        number_of_bedrooms + number_of_bathrooms + total_area +
                        quality_grade + 
                        factor(zip_code), # neighborhood effects (via zip code for now)
                      data = props_i676_tomodel)

model_i676_more_summary <- summary(model_i676_more)
model_i676_more_RMSE <- getRMSE(model_i676_more)
# log_dist_highway                             0.101134640
# Multiple R-squared:  0.3585,	Adjusted R-squared:  0.3421

# create a clean table to show model results
model_i676_more_table <- data.frame(model_i676_more_summary$coefficients) %>% 
  rename(p = `Pr...t..`) %>% 
  select(Estimate, p) %>% 
  mutate(Estimate = round(Estimate, 3),
         p = round(p, 3))
row.names(model_i676_more_table) <- c("Intercept", "Log Dist. to I-676", "Residential", "Building Code - Least Exp.", "Building Code - More Exp.", "Building Code - Most Exp.", "Zoning - CMX3, 4", "Zoning - CMX5", "Zoning - ICMX", "Zoning - IRMX", "Zoning - Other", "Zoning - RM", "Zoning - RMX3", "Zoning - RSA5", "Year Built - New", "Year Built - Post-War Mid", "Year Built - Pre-War", "Year Built - Unknown", "Central Air - Unknown", "Central Air - Yes", "1 Bedrooms", "2 Bedrooms", "3 Bedrooms", "4 Bedrooms", "5 Bedrooms", "Unknown Num. Bedrooms", "1 Bathrooms", "2 Bathrooms", "3-5 Bathrooms", "6 Bathrooms", "7 Bathrooms", "Unknown Num. Bathrooms", "Total Area", "Quality Grade - Below Average", "Quality Grade - Good", "ZIP code - 19106", "ZIP code - 19107", "ZIP code - 19123", "ZIP code - 19130")

model_i676_more_table %>% 
  kbl(align = c("l", rep("c", 2)),
      caption = "Regression Results: Log Price ~ Log Distance to I-676 and Other Predictors",
      col.names = c("Estimate", "p value")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>%
  row_spec(2, bold = T, background = "#7fe3d6") %>% 
  add_footnote(label = paste0("Adj. R-squared: ", round(model_i676_more_summary$adj.r.squared, 3), ", RMSE: ", round(model_i676_more_RMSE, 3)),
               notation = "none")

```

Finally, we look at a more robust model (which is still relatively simple, including only internal features of the property in addition to ZIP code and logged distance to [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}). This model includes the following predictors: year_built_group (categorical), quality_grade (categorical), number_of_bathrooms (categorical), number_of_bedrooms (categorical), total_area (continuous), central_air (categorical), building_code (categorical), zoning group (categorical), and a variable dictating whether the property is residential or not (binary). This more complex model does a better job at explaining the variance in property price than our previous two models, but is not optimal either. The **adjusted R-squared** for this model is **`r round(model_i676_more_summary$adj.r.squared, 3)`** and our **RMSE** is **`r round(model_i676_more_RMSE, 3)`**. 

When including these other predictors, the **effect of logged distance to [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} decreases** but remains statistically significant (beta coefficient of `r model_i676_more_table$Estimate[2]`). This means that for every 1% increase in distance from the highway, property price increases by `r paste0(round(abs(1.01^model_i676_more_table$Estimate[2] - 1), 4)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, this means that if a property that is \$100,000 is 50m away from the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway to be about **`r paste0("$", round((4^model_i676_more_table$Estimate[2])*650000) - 650000)` more expensive** (`r round(100*((4^model_i676_more_table$Estimate[2])*650000 - 650000)/650000, 1)` % change).

#### Model Predictions to look at price changes

```{r i676_predtable}
distances <- seq(50, 250, by = 50)

# model predictions
pred_i676_simple <- exp(predict(model_i676, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_highway = log(distances))))

# this complicated model needs more parameters
# where possible, i use the median value, otherwise the most common value for these other control variables
pred_i676_more <- exp(predict(model_i676_more, 
                              newdata = data.frame(
                                log_dist_highway = log(distances),
                                residential = 1,
                                building_code_description_new = "LeastExpensive",
                                zoning_group = "CMX(3,4)",
                                year_built_group = "Pre-War",
                                central_air = "Unknown",
                                number_of_bedrooms = "0",
                                number_of_bathrooms = "0",
                                total_area = 0,
                                quality_grade = "Below Average",
                                zip_code = "19107")
                              ))

# get predicted price changes from philly scale analysis
i676_pred_table <- data.frame(
  Analysis_Scale = "I-676 Effects in Study Area",
  Distance_m = distances,
  HighwayOnly_Prices = round(pred_i676_simple),
  HighwayPlus_Prices = round(pred_i676_more),
  Chng_HighwayOnly_Prices = round(pred_i676_simple - pred_i676_simple[1]),
  Chng_HighwayPlus_Prices = round(pred_i676_more - pred_i676_more[1]),
  PercChng_HighwayOnly_Prices = round(100*(pred_i676_simple - pred_i676_simple[1]) / pred_i676_simple[1], 1),
  PercChng_HighwayPlus_Prices = round(100*(pred_i676_more - pred_i676_more[1]) / pred_i676_more[1], 1)
)
i676_pred_table %>% 
  kbl(align = "c",
      caption = "Regression Predictions for I-676 Effects",
      col.names = c("Analysis Scale", "Distance (m)", "Highway Only Prices", "Highway Plus Prices", "Change Highway Only Prices", "Change Highway Plus Prices", "% Change Highway Only Prices", "% Change Highway Plus Prices")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  row_spec(c(1,3), bold = T, background = "#7fe3d6")

```

### Discontinuity Effects

To complicate things even more, within our study area, we see that proximity to [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} has **different effects** on the [North (Callowhill)]{style="color: #eb5600;"} and [South (Chinatown)]{style="color: #1a9988;"} sides.

```{r discontinuity_data, quiet = TRUE, results = 'hide'}
# with most recently updated data (990 properties)
discontinuity_plot_ungrouped <- props_i676_tomodel %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(distance_to_I676m = distance_to_I676 * 0.3048,
         distance_to_highway = case_when(
           I676_NS == "north" ~ distance_to_I676m,
           I676_NS == "south" ~ -distance_to_I676m
           ))

discontinuity_plot <- discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
  group_by(distance_to_highway, I676_NS) %>%
  summarise(mean_log_price = mean(log_price, na.rm = T), .groups = "drop")

# median property prices on each side
med_north <- round(median(discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                      filter(I676_NS == "north") %>% 
                      pull(adj_sale_price)))

med_south <- round(median(discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                      filter(I676_NS == "south") %>% 
                      pull(adj_sale_price)))

# range of property prices on each side
range_north <- round(range(discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                      filter(I676_NS == "north") %>% 
                      pull(adj_sale_price)))

range_south <- round(range(discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                      filter(I676_NS == "south") %>% 
                      pull(adj_sale_price)))

```

In the plot above, we see that on the [North side]{style="color: #eb5600;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property prices remain relatively stable and unaffected by distance to the highway. The median property price in the [North]{style="color: #eb5600;"} is `r paste0("$", substr(med_north, 1, 3), ",", substr(med_north, 4, 6))`. When predicting logged property price, the beta coefficient for distance to highway is `r coef_north`, meaning the **highway has no effect on the price**.

On the other hand, in the [South side]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property prices are within the same range of prices as in the [North side]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, but the median property price is slightly higher at `r paste0("$", substr(med_south, 1, 3), ",", substr(med_south, 4, 6))`. When predicting logged property price to the [South]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of the highway, the beta coefficient for distance to highway is `r coef_south`, meaning **distance to highway has a very small, positive effect on the price**. For every 1m increase in distance from [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(exp(coef_south)-1, 3)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, a property that is \$100,000 and 50m [South]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} would be about **`r paste0("$", round((exp(coef_south)^150)*100000) - 100000)` more expensive** a block further from the highway.

#### Interpretation with median price of $650,000 and 200m away

In the plot above, we see that on the [North side]{style="color: #eb5600;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property prices remain relatively stable and unaffected by distance to the highway. The median property price in the [North]{style="color: #eb5600;"} is `r paste0("$", substr(med_north, 1, 3), ",", substr(med_north, 4, 6))`. When predicting logged property price, the beta coefficient for distance to highway is `r coef_north`, meaning the **highway has no effect on the price**. More precisely, for a property that is \$650,000 (median price of properties between 45-55m from I-676) and 50m [north]{style="color: #eb5600;"} of the highway, we can expect a similar property a block further from the highway (assuming a block is about 200m) to be about **`r paste0("$", round(650000 - (exp(coef_north_all)^150)*650000))` cheaper** (`r round(100*((exp(coef_north_all)^150)*650000 - 650000)/650000, 1)` % change).

On the other hand, in the [South side]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property prices are within the same range of prices as in the [North side]{style="color: #eb5600;"}, but the median property price is slightly higher at `r paste0("$", substr(med_south, 1, 3), ",", substr(med_south, 4, 6))`. When predicting logged property price to the [South]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of the highway, the beta coefficient for distance to highway is `r coef_south`, meaning **distance to highway has a positive effect on the price**. For every 1m increase in distance from [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}, property price increases by `r paste0(round(exp(coef_south_all)-1, 3)*100,"%")`. In more understandable terms, a property that is \$650,000 and 50m [South]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"} would be about **`r paste0("$", round((exp(coef_south_all)^150)*650000) - 650000)` more expensive** a block further from the highway (`r round(100*((exp(coef_south_all)^150)*650000 - 650000)/650000, 1)` % change).

#### Model Predictions to look at Price change

```{r disc_predtable}
# models (redoing them because i want to use log_dist_highway)
i676_north <- lm(log_price ~ log_dist_highway,
                 data = discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                   filter(I676_NS == "north"))

i676_south <- lm(log_price ~ abs(log_dist_highway),
                 data = discontinuity_plot_ungrouped %>% 
                   filter(I676_NS == "south"))

distances <- seq(50, 250, by = 50)

# model predictions
pred_i676_n <- exp(predict(i676_north, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_highway = log(distances))))

pred_i676_s <- exp(predict(i676_south, newdata = data.frame(log_dist_highway = log(distances))))

# get predicted price changes from philly scale analysis
i676NS_pred_table <- data.frame(
  Analysis_Scale = "I-676 Effects -- North/South",
  Distance_m = distances,
  HighwayOnly_Prices = round(pred_i676_n),
  HighwayPlus_Prices = round(pred_i676_s),
  Chng_HighwayOnly_Prices = round(pred_i676_n - pred_i676_n[1]),
  Chng_HighwayPlus_Prices = round(pred_i676_s - pred_i676_s[1]),
  PercChng_HighwayOnly_Prices = round(100*(pred_i676_n - pred_i676_n[1]) / pred_i676_n[1], 1),
  PercChng_HighwayPlus_Prices = round(100*(pred_i676_s - pred_i676_s[1]) / pred_i676_s[1], 1)
)
i676NS_pred_table %>% 
  kbl(align = "c",
      caption = "Regression Predictions for I-676 Effects -- North/South",
      col.names = c("Analysis Scale", "Distance (m)", "North of I-676 Prices", "South of I-676 Prices", "Change North of I-676 Prices", "Change South of I-676 Prices", "% Change North of I-676 Prices", "% Change South of I-676 Prices")) %>% 
  kable_styling() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria") %>% 
  row_spec(c(1,3), bold = T, background = "#7fe3d6")

```


This demonstrates that in our study area, the **highway has a very small influence on property price** that is only really seen on the [South side]{style="color: #1a9988;"} of [I-676]{style="color: #7fe3d6;"}.

### Zoning-Based Price Effects
```{r highway_effects_zoning, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
property_filtered <- property_final
property_filtered <- st_as_sf(property_filtered, sf_column_name = "geometry")

avg_price_zoning <- property_filtered %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%  
  group_by(zoning) %>%
  summarise(avg_price_zoning = mean(adj_sale_price, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

property_filtered <- property_filtered %>%
  left_join(avg_price_zoning, by = "zoning")%>%
  filter(location != "711-39 SPRING GARDEN ST")

property_filtered <- property_filtered %>%
  mutate(zoning_group = case_when(
    zoning %in% c("CMX5", "ICMX") ~ "High-Density Commercial",
    zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "Residential Industrial",
    zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM4", "RMX3", "RSA5") ~ "Residential",
    zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "Neighborhood Commercial",
    zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "Community Commercial",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ))

avg_price_group <- property_filtered %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(zoning_group) %>%
  summarise(avg_adj_sale_price = mean(adj_sale_price, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

property_filtered <- property_filtered %>%
  left_join(avg_price_group, by = "zoning_group")


ggplot(property_filtered %>% filter(!is.na(zoning_group) & zoning_group != "Other"), 
       aes(x = log1p(distance_to_I676), y = log1p(adj_sale_price))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5, color = "#1B8370") + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#E4572E") +
  facet_wrap(~ zoning_group, scales = "free") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "                      Zoning wise Relationship Between Distance to I-676 and Sales Price", 
       x = "Distance to I-676", 
       y = "Sale Price")
```

```{r FE countinued}
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("SPPOA") ~ "SPPOA",
      zoning %in% c("I2") ~ "I2",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )

mean_depth <- mean(property_CT$depth, na.rm = TRUE)
property_CT$depth[is.na(property_CT$depth)] <- mean_depth

st_write(property_CT, "property_CT_FE.geojson", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

```{r discontinuity plot s0}
#property_S0 <- st_transform(property_S0, 2272)
property_S1_4326 <- st_read("Storymap_dataset/property_S1_4326.geojson")
property_S0 <- st_transform(property_S1_4326, 2272)   # yes use property_S1_4326 and the field we use here is adj_sale_price

discontinuity_S0 <- property_S0 %>% 
  filter(adj_sale_price > 100)
discontinuity_S0 <- rbind(
  discontinuity_S0 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_north["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "north"),
  discontinuity_S0 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_south["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "south")
)

discontinuity_S0 <- discontinuity_S0 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(
    distance_to_I676m = distance_to_I676 * 0.3048,
    distance_to_highway = case_when(
      I676_NS == "north" ~ distance_to_I676m,
      I676_NS == "south" ~ -distance_to_I676m
    )
  )

discontinuity_S0 <- discontinuity_S0 %>% 
  filter(abs(distance_to_highway) <= 500)

coef_north_S0 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(adj_sale_price+1) ~ distance_to_highway,
       data = discontinuity_S0,
       subset = I676_NS == "north"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)

coef_south_S0 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(adj_sale_price+1) ~ abs(distance_to_highway),
       data = discontinuity_S0,
       subset = I676_NS == "south"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)
discontinuity_plot_S0 <- ggplot(data = discontinuity_S0) +
  geom_point(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(adj_sale_price+1), color = I676_NS), size = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(adj_sale_price+1), color = I676_NS),
              method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("north" = "#eb5600", "south" = "#1a9988")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "None",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = 'Highway Effect - Scenario 0', 
    subtitle = glue("<span style='color:#1a9988;'>South Side</span> vs. <span style='color:#eb5600;'>North Side</span>"),
    x = "Distance to the Highway (m)",
    y = "Sale Price"
  ) +
  geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 11.5, label = "I-676"),
             fill = "black", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_north_S0,
                x = 250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#eb5600",
            show.legend = F) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_south_S0,
                x = -250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#1a9988",
            show.legend = F)
```

```{r scenario 1 data processing, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
grocery <- readRDS("Dataset/poi/poi_grocery.rds")
res_poi <- readRDS("Dataset/poi/poi_restaurant.rds")

property_proj <- st_transform(property_sf, 2272)

restaurant_proj <- st_transform(res_poi, 2272)

grocery_idx <- st_nearest_feature(property_proj, grocery_proj)

property_proj$nearest_grocery_name <- grocery_proj$name[grocery_idx]
property_proj$nearest_grocery_dist <- st_distance(
  property_proj,
  grocery_proj[grocery_idx, ],
  by_element = TRUE
)
restaurant_idx <- st_nearest_feature(property_proj, restaurant_proj)
property_proj$nearest_restaurant_name <- restaurant_proj$name[restaurant_idx]
property_proj$nearest_restaurant_dist <- st_distance(
  property_proj,
  restaurant_proj[restaurant_idx, ],
  by_element = TRUE
)
property_proj$nearest_grocery_dist_m <- as.numeric(property_proj$nearest_grocery_dist)
property_proj$nearest_restaurant_dist_m <- as.numeric(property_proj$nearest_restaurant_dist)
clean_property_poi_distances <- function(property_sf) {
  property_sf %>%
    mutate(
      nearest_grocery_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_grocery_dist),
      nearest_restaurant_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_restaurant_dist)) %>%
    select(
      -nearest_grocery_dist,
      -nearest_restaurant_dist
    )
}

property1_final <- clean_property_poi_distances(property_proj)

calculate_nearest_distance <- function(set_points, other_layer) {
  nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(set_points, other_layer)
  st_distance(set_points, other_layer[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE) %>% as.numeric()
}
```

```{r}
    landuse = case_when(

      landuse %in% c("Commercial Consumer", "Commercial Mixed Residential",
                     "Industrial", "Transportation", "Culture/Amusement") ~ "Commercial",
      landuse %in% c("Civic/Institution", "Residential High") ~ "Residential High/Civic",
      TRUE ~ landuse
    ),
    # Year Built
    year_built = as.numeric(year_built),
    year_built_missing = ifelse(is.na(year_built), 1, 0),
#    year_built = case_when(
#      is.na(year_built) ~ "Unknown",
#      TRUE ~ as.character(year_built)
#    ),
#    year_built = factor(year_built),
    year_built_group = case_when(
       is.na(year_built) ~ "Unknown",
       year_built < 1940 ~ "Pre-War",
       year_built < 2000 ~ "Post-War Mid",
       year_built < 2020 ~ "Modern",
       year_built >= 2020 ~ "New"
    ),
    year_built_group = factor(year_built_group, levels = c("Pre-War", "Post-War Mid", "Modern", "New", "Unknown")),
    # Log Transforms
    log_price = log(sale_price),
    log_dist_highway = log(distance_to_I676 + 1),

    # Central Air
    central_air = case_when(
      central_air %in% c("Y", "1")  ~ "Y",
      central_air %in% c("N", "0") ~ "N",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    central_air = factor(central_air),
    central_air_missing = ifelse(central_air == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Garage Spaces
    garage_spaces_missing = ifelse(is.na(garage_spaces), 1, 0),
    garage_spaces = case_when(
#      is.na(garage_spaces) ~ "Unknown",
      garage_spaces == 0 | garage_spaces == 1 ~ "less than 2",
      TRUE ~ "2 or more"
    ),
    garage_spaces = factor(garage_spaces),

    # Bedrooms
    number_of_bedrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bedrooms)),
    number_of_bedrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bedrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), median_bedroom, number_of_bedrooms),
    number_of_bedrooms = case_when(
      is.na(number_of_bedrooms) ~ "Unknown",
      number_of_bedrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bedrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(2, 3) ~ "2",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(5, 6) ~ "3",
      number_of_bedrooms == 4 ~"4",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(7, 9, 12) ~ "5"
    ),
    number_of_bedrooms = factor(number_of_bedrooms),

    # Bathrooms
    number_of_bathrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bathrooms)),
    number_of_bathrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bathrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), median_bathroom, number_of_bathrooms),
    number_of_bathrooms = case_when(
      number_of_bathrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bathrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bathrooms == 2 ~ "2",
      number_of_bathrooms %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "3-5",
      number_of_bathrooms == 6 ~ "6",
      number_of_bathrooms == 7 ~ "7",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    number_of_bathrooms = factor(number_of_bathrooms),

    # Total Livable Area
    total_livable_area = ifelse(is.na(total_livable_area) | total_livable_area == 1, 0, total_livable_area),

    # Quality Grade
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("A ", "A-") | is.na(quality_grade) ~ "Good",
      quality_grade %in% c("3 ", "C+", "C")  ~ "Average",
      TRUE ~ "Below Average"
    ),
    quality_grade = factor(quality_grade, levels = c("Good", "Average", "Below Average")),
    quality_grade_missing = ifelse(is.na(quality_grade), 1, 0),

    # Construction
    general_construction = as.character(general_construction),
    general_construction = case_when(
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ general_construction
    ),
    general_construction = factor(general_construction),
    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities
    separate_utilities = case_when(
      is.na(separate_utilities) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ separate_utilities
    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7) | is.na(exterior_condition) ~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,2,7) | is.na(interior_condition) ~ "Good",
      interior_condition %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),

    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("SPPOA") ~ "SPPOA",
      zoning %in% c("I2") ~ "I2",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )

mean_depth <- mean(property_S1_fe$depth, na.rm = TRUE)
property_S1_fe$depth[is.na(property_S1_fe$depth)] <- mean_depth
```

```{r predictive modeling for scenario 1, quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
  ) %>%
  select(
    log_dist_highway,
    log_distance_to_city_hall,
    log_nearest_restaurant_dist_m,
    log_distance_to_nearest_park,
    zoning_group,
    zip_code,

    central_air,
    year_built_group,
    LPSS_PER1000,
    general_construction,
    garage_spaces,
    separate_utilities,
    category_code,
    crime_nn5,
    nhoods_name,
    landuse,
    Longitude, Latitude
  )
```

```{r data processing for S2 S3 S4}
      TRUE ~ interior_condition
    ),
    landuse = landuse_new,
    category_code = category_code_new,
    zoning = zoning_new
  )
```

```{r discontinuity plot s1}
property_S1 <- st_transform(property_S1_predict, 2272)

discontinuity_S1_predict <- property_S1 %>% 
  filter(predicted_price > 100)

discontinuity_S1_predict <- rbind(
  discontinuity_S1_predict %>% st_intersection(studyarea_north["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "north"),
  discontinuity_S1_predict %>% st_intersection(studyarea_south["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "south")
)

discontinuity_S1_predict <- discontinuity_S1_predict %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(
    distance_to_I676m = distance_to_I676 * 0.3048,
    distance_to_highway = case_when(
      I676_NS == "north" ~ distance_to_I676m,
      I676_NS == "south" ~ -distance_to_I676m
    )
  )

discontinuity_S1_predict <- discontinuity_S1_predict %>% 
  filter(abs(distance_to_highway) <= 500)

coef_north_S1 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(predicted_price+1) ~ distance_to_highway,
       data = discontinuity_S1_predict,
       subset = I676_NS == "north"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)

coef_south_S1 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(predicted_price+1) ~ abs(distance_to_highway),
       data = discontinuity_S1_predict,
       subset = I676_NS == "south"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)

discontinuity_plot_S1 <- ggplot(data = discontinuity_S1_predict) +
  geom_point(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(predicted_price+1), color = I676_NS), size = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(predicted_price+1), color = I676_NS),
              method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("north" = "#eb5600", "south" = "#1a9988")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "None",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = 'Highway Effect - Scenario 1', 
    subtitle = glue("<span style='color:#1a9988;'>South Side</span> vs. <span style='color:#eb5600;'>North Side</span>"),
    x = "Distance to the Highway (m)",
    y = "Sale Price"
  ) +
  geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 11.5, label = "I-676"),
             fill = "black", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_north_S1,
                x = 250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#eb5600",
            show.legend = F) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_south_S1,
                x = -250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#1a9988",
            show.legend = F)
discontinuity_plot_S1

ggsave(
```

```{r S2-FE countinued , quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
    # Bedrooms
    number_of_bedrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bedrooms)),
    number_of_bedrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bedrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), median_bedroom, number_of_bedrooms),
    number_of_bedrooms = case_when(
      is.na(number_of_bedrooms) ~ "Unknown",
      number_of_bedrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bedrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(2, 3) ~ "2",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(5, 6) ~ "3",
      number_of_bedrooms == 4 ~"4",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(7, 9, 12) ~ "5"
    ),
    number_of_bedrooms = factor(number_of_bedrooms),

    # Bathrooms
    number_of_bathrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bathrooms)),
    number_of_bathrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bathrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), median_bathroom, number_of_bathrooms),
    number_of_bathrooms = case_when(
      number_of_bathrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bathrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bathrooms == 2 ~ "2",
      number_of_bathrooms %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "3-5",
      number_of_bathrooms == 6 ~ "6",
      number_of_bathrooms == 7 ~ "7",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    number_of_bathrooms = factor(number_of_bathrooms),

    # Total Livable Area
    total_livable_area = ifelse(is.na(total_livable_area) | total_livable_area == 1, 0, total_livable_area),

    # Quality Grade
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("A ", "A-") | is.na(quality_grade) ~ "Good",
      quality_grade %in% c("3 ", "C+", "C")  ~ "Average",
      TRUE ~ "Below Average"
    ),
    quality_grade = factor(quality_grade, levels = c("Good", "Average", "Below Average")),
    quality_grade_missing = ifelse(is.na(quality_grade), 1, 0),

    # Construction
    general_construction = as.character(general_construction),
    general_construction = case_when(
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ general_construction
    ),
    general_construction = factor(general_construction),
    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities
    separate_utilities = case_when(
      is.na(separate_utilities) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ separate_utilities
    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7) | is.na(exterior_condition) ~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,2,7) | is.na(interior_condition) ~ "Good",
      interior_condition %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),

    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",
      zoning %in% c("SPPOA") ~ "SPPOA",
      zoning %in% c("I2") ~ "I2",
      zoning %in% c("CMX2.5", "CMX2", "CMX1") ~ "CMX(1,2,2.5)",
      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    zoning_group = factor(zoning_group),

    zoning = case_when(
      is.na(zoning) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ zoning
    ),
    zoning = factor(zoning),
    zip_code = factor(zip_code)
  )

mean_depth <- mean(property_S2_fe$depth, na.rm = TRUE)
property_S2_fe$depth[is.na(property_S2_fe$depth)] <- mean_depth
```

### Alternate Commercial - discontinuity plot
```{r Alternate Commercial - discontinuity plot}
property_S2 <- st_transform(property_S2_predict, 2272)

discontinuity_S2 <- property_S2 %>% 
  filter(predicted_price > 100)  # 注意这里用 predicted_price，不是 adj_sale_price

discontinuity_S2 <- rbind(
  discontinuity_S2 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_north["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "north"),
  discontinuity_S2 %>% st_intersection(studyarea_south["geometry"]) %>%
    mutate(I676_NS = "south")
)

discontinuity_S2 <- discontinuity_S2 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(distance_to_I676m = distance_to_I676 * 0.3048,
         distance_to_highway = case_when(
           I676_NS == "north" ~ distance_to_I676m,
           I676_NS == "south" ~ -distance_to_I676m
         ))
discontinuity_S2 <- discontinuity_S2 %>% 
  filter(abs(distance_to_highway) <= 500)

coef_north_S2 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(predicted_price+1) ~ distance_to_highway,
       data = discontinuity_S2,
       I676_NS == "north"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)

coef_south_S2 <- round(
  summary(
    lm(log(predicted_price+1) ~ abs(distance_to_highway),
       data = discontinuity_S2,
       I676_NS == "south"))$coefficients[2,1], 3)

discontinuity_plot_S2 <- ggplot(data = discontinuity_S2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(predicted_price+1), color = I676_NS), size = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = distance_to_highway, y = log(predicted_price+1), color = I676_NS), method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("north" = "#eb5600", "south" = "#1a9988")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "None",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 12),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)) +
  labs(title = 'Highway Effect - Scenario 2', 
       subtitle = glue("<span style='color:#1a9988;'>South Side</span> vs. <span style='color:#eb5600;'>North Side</span>"),
       x = "Distance to the Highway (m)",
       y = "Sale Price") +
  geom_label(aes(x = 0, y = 11.5, label = "I-676"),
             fill = "black", color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_north_S2,
                x = 250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#eb5600",
            show.legend = F) +
  geom_text(aes(label = coef_south_S2,
                x = -250,
                y = 11.825),
            color = "#1a9988",
            show.legend = F)

discontinuity_plot_S2

)
```

```{r S3-FE countinued , quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
    number_of_bathrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), median_bathroom, number_of_bathrooms),
```

```{r S4-FE countinued , quiet=TRUE, results='hide'}
median_bedroom <- median(as.numeric(as.character(property_S4_no_fe$number_of_bedrooms)), na.rm = TRUE)
median_bathroom <- median(as.numeric(as.character(property_S4_no_fe$number_of_bathrooms)), na.rm = TRUE)

#  filter(!zoning %in% c("I2", "SPPOA"))%>%
  mutate(
        # Neighborhood Name
    nhoods_name = case_when(
      nhoods_name %in% c("CENTER_CITY", "LOGAN_SQUARE") ~ "WEST_PART",
      TRUE ~ nhoods_name
    ),

    # Land Use
    landuse = case_when(
      landuse %in% c("Park/Open Space", "Other/Unknown", "Commercial Business/Professional") ~ "Open Space/Business",
      landuse %in% c("Commercial Consumer", "Commercial Mixed Residential",
                     "Industrial", "Transportation", "Culture/Amusement") ~ "Commercial",
      landuse %in% c("Civic/Institution", "Residential High") ~ "Residential High/Civic",
      TRUE ~ landuse
    ),
    # Year Built
    year_built = as.numeric(year_built),
    year_built_missing = ifelse(is.na(year_built), 1, 0),
#    year_built = case_when(
#      is.na(year_built) ~ "Unknown",
#      TRUE ~ as.character(year_built)
#    ),
#    year_built = factor(year_built),
    year_built_group = case_when(
       is.na(year_built) ~ "Unknown",
       year_built < 1940 ~ "Pre-War",
       year_built < 2000 ~ "Post-War Mid",
       year_built < 2020 ~ "Modern",
       year_built >= 2020 ~ "New"
    ),
    year_built_group = factor(year_built_group, levels = c("Pre-War", "Post-War Mid", "Modern", "New", "Unknown")),
    # Log Transforms
    log_price = log(sale_price),
    log_dist_highway = log(distance_to_I676 + 1),

    # Central Air
    central_air = case_when(
      central_air %in% c("Y", "1")  ~ "Y",
      central_air %in% c("N", "0") ~ "N",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    central_air = factor(central_air),
    central_air_missing = ifelse(central_air == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Garage Spaces
    garage_spaces_missing = ifelse(is.na(garage_spaces), 1, 0),
    garage_spaces = case_when(
#      is.na(garage_spaces) ~ "Unknown",
      garage_spaces == 0 | garage_spaces == 1 ~ "less than 2",
      TRUE ~ "2 or more"
    ),
    garage_spaces = factor(garage_spaces),

    # Bedrooms
    number_of_bedrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bedrooms)),
    number_of_bedrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bedrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bedrooms), median_bedroom, number_of_bedrooms),
    number_of_bedrooms = case_when(
      is.na(number_of_bedrooms) ~ "Unknown",
      number_of_bedrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bedrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(2, 3) ~ "2",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(5, 6) ~ "3",
      number_of_bedrooms == 4 ~"4",
      number_of_bedrooms %in% c(7, 9, 12) ~ "5"
    ),
    number_of_bedrooms = factor(number_of_bedrooms),

    # Bathrooms
    number_of_bathrooms = as.numeric(as.character(number_of_bathrooms)),
    number_of_bathrooms_missing = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), 1, 0),
    number_of_bathrooms_filled = ifelse(is.na(number_of_bathrooms), median_bathroom, number_of_bathrooms),
    number_of_bathrooms = case_when(
      number_of_bathrooms == 0 ~ "0",
      number_of_bathrooms == 1 ~ "1",
      number_of_bathrooms == 2 ~ "2",
      number_of_bathrooms %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "3-5",
      number_of_bathrooms == 6 ~ "6",
      number_of_bathrooms == 7 ~ "7",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    number_of_bathrooms = factor(number_of_bathrooms),

    # Total Livable Area
    total_livable_area = ifelse(is.na(total_livable_area) | total_livable_area == 1, 0, total_livable_area),

    # Quality Grade
    quality_grade = case_when(
      quality_grade %in% c("A ", "A-") | is.na(quality_grade) ~ "Good",
      quality_grade %in% c("3 ", "C+", "C")  ~ "Average",
      TRUE ~ "Below Average"
    ),
    quality_grade = factor(quality_grade, levels = c("Good", "Average", "Below Average")),
    quality_grade_missing = ifelse(is.na(quality_grade), 1, 0),

    # Construction
    general_construction = as.character(general_construction),
    general_construction = case_when(
      is.na(general_construction) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ general_construction
    ),
    general_construction = factor(general_construction),
    general_construction_missing = ifelse(general_construction == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Separate Utilities
    separate_utilities = case_when(
      is.na(separate_utilities) ~ "Unknown",
      TRUE ~ separate_utilities
    ),
    separate_utilities = factor(separate_utilities, levels = c("A", "B", "C", "Unknown")),
    separate_utilities_missing = ifelse(separate_utilities == "Unknown", 1, 0),

    # Exterior Condition
    exterior_condition = case_when(
      exterior_condition == 2 ~ "Good",
      exterior_condition %in% c(1, 6, 7) | is.na(exterior_condition) ~ "Average",
      exterior_condition %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Below Average"
 #     TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    exterior_condition = factor(exterior_condition),

    # Interior Condition
    interior_condition = case_when(
      interior_condition %in% c(1,2,7) | is.na(interior_condition) ~ "Good",
      interior_condition %in% c(3,4,5) ~ "Average",
      interior_condition %in% c(6) ~ "Below Average",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    interior_condition = factor(interior_condition),

    # Category Code
    category_code_original = as.character(category_code),
    category_code_group = case_when(
      category_code == "12" ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "14" ~ "2 ",
      category_code == "10" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "15" ~ "5 ",
      category_code == "16" ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "7 "  ~ "4 ",
      category_code == "8 "  ~ "6 ",
      category_code == "9 "  ~ "2 ",
      category_code %in% c("1 ", "2 ", "3 ", "4 ", "5 ", "6 ") ~ category_code,
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    category_code = factor(category_code_group),

    # Zoning
    zoning_group = case_when(
      zoning %in% c("CMX5") ~ "CMX5",
      zoning %in% c("IRMX") ~ "IRMX",
      zoning %in% c("RM1", "RM2", "RM4") ~ "RM",
      zoning %in% c("RMX3") ~ "RMX3",
      zoning %in% c("RSA5") ~ "RSA5",
      zoning %in% c("ICMX") ~ "ICMX",

      zoning %in% c("CMX3", "CMX4") ~ "CMX(3,4)",

    ),

    zoning = case_when(
```

######## here is the price changes 100m away from i676 for all scenarios, unorganized version for your exploration
```{r S0 - price change}
get_price_change_table <- function(data, price_col, scenario_label) {
  formula_all   <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ distance_to_highway"))
  formula_south <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ abs(distance_to_highway)"))
  formula_north <- as.formula(paste0("log(", price_col, " + 1) ~ distance_to_highway"))
  lm_all   <- lm(formula_all,   data = data)
  lm_south <- lm(formula_south, data = data %>% filter(I676_NS == "south"))
  lm_north <- lm(formula_north, data = data %>% filter(I676_NS == "north"))

  distances <- seq(50, 200, by = 50)
  pred_all   <- exp(predict(lm_all,   newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = distances))) - 1
  pred_south <- exp(predict(lm_south, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = distances))) - 1
  pred_north <- exp(predict(lm_north, newdata = data.frame(distance_to_highway = distances))) - 1
  tibble(
    Scenario        = scenario_label,
    Distance_m      = distances,
    South_Price     = round(pred_south),
    North_Price     = round(pred_north),
    Overall_Price   = round(pred_all),
    South_Change    = round(pred_south - pred_south[1]),
    North_Change    = round(pred_north - pred_north[1]),
    Overall_Change  = round(pred_all - pred_all[1])
  )
}
S0_table <- get_price_change_table(discontinuity_S0, "adj_sale_price", "Scenario 0")
S0_table %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Distance-Based Price Summary (Scenario 0)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

price change calculations 
scenario 0 vs. 1
```{r}
property_S1_perc_change <- property_S1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_sale_price), adj_sale_price > 100) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = round((predicted_price - adj_sale_price) / adj_sale_price * 100, 1),
    perc_bucket = case_when(
      perc_change < -10  ~ "< -10%",
      perc_change < 0    ~ "-10% to 0%",
      perc_change < 10   ~ "0% to +10%",
      perc_change < 50   ~ "+10% to +50%",
      perc_change < 100  ~ "+50 % to +100%",
      perc_change < 200  ~ "+100% to +200%",
      TRUE               ~ "> 200%"
    ),
    perc_bucket = factor(perc_bucket,
                         levels = c("< -10%", "-10% to 0%", "0% to +10%",
                                    "+10% to +50%","+50 % to +100%", "+100% to +200%", "> 200%")),
    size_bucket = case_when(
      perc_bucket == "< -10%"        ~ 1.5,
      perc_bucket == "-10% to 0%"    ~ 2,
      perc_bucket == "0% to +10%"    ~ 2.5,
      perc_bucket == "+10% to +50%"  ~ 4,
      perc_bucket == "+50 % to +100%" ~ 5,
      perc_bucket == "+50% to +200%" ~ 6,
      perc_bucket == "> 200%"        ~ 7
    ),
    property_category = case_when(
      category_code_chain %in% c("3:Mixed Use", "4:Commercial") ~ "Commercial",
      category_code_chain %in% c("1:Single Family", "2:Multi Family", "14:Apartments > 4 units") ~ "Residential",
      category_code_chain == "15:Retail" ~ "Retail",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(property_category)) %>%
  mutate(property_category = factor(property_category, levels = c("Commercial", "Residential", "Retail"))) %>%
  select(
    parcel_number, objectid, perc_change, perc_bucket, size_bucket, geometry,
    predicted_price, zoning, category_code, landuse, property_category, everything()
  )
mapview(property_S1_perc_change,
        zcol = "perc_bucket",
        cex = property_S1_perc_change$size_bucket * 2,
        alpha = 0.8,
        col.regions = c("#06402B","#008B8B","#CDB902","#FFB343", "#F8A58E","#CD1C18", "#660033"),
        stroke = FALSE,
        legend = TRUE,
        layer.name = "S0 vs S1: Sale Price % Change")

st_write(property_S1_perc_change,"~/Documents/Upenn/Practicum/2025/Chinatown-Practicum-my/finalresults/property_s0_s1.json", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)

```

scenario 1 vs. 2:要不要把
```{r}
mapviewOptions(viewer.suppress = FALSE)

price_change_s1s2 <- property_S1_perc_change %>%
  filter(!is.na(adj_sale_price), adj_sale_price > 100) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(objectid, predicted_price_s1 = predicted_price) %>%
  inner_join(
    property_S2_perc_change %>%
      select(objectid, parcel_number, location, landuse, category_code, zoning, alternate_feature, geometry, predicted_price_s2 = predicted_price),
    by = "objectid"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = round((predicted_price_s2 - predicted_price_s1) / predicted_price_s1 * 100, 1),

    perc_bucket = case_when(
      perc_change < 0     ~ "< 0%",
      perc_change == 0    ~ "0%",
      perc_change <= 10    ~ "0–10%",
      perc_change <= 30   ~ "10–30%",
      perc_change <= 50   ~ "30–50%",
      TRUE                ~ "50%-60%"
    ),
    perc_bucket = factor(perc_bucket,
                         levels = c("< 0%", "0%", "0–10%", "10–30%", "30–50%", "50%-60%")),

    size_bucket = case_when(
      perc_bucket == "< 0%"    ~ 2,
      perc_bucket == "0%"      ~ 2.5,
      perc_bucket == "0–10%"    ~ 3,
      perc_bucket == "10–30%"   ~ 4,
      perc_bucket == "30–50%"  ~ 5,
      perc_bucket == "50%-60%"   ~ 6
    )
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry", crs = st_crs(property_S2))

mapview(price_change_s1s2,
        zcol = "perc_bucket",
        cex = price_change_s1s2$size_bucket*2,
        alpha = 0.5,
        col.regions = c("#06402B","#CDB902","#FFB343", "#F8A58E","#CD1C18", "#660033"),
        stroke = FALSE,
        legend = TRUE,
        layer.name = "S1 vs. S2: Sale Price % Change")

st_write(price_change_s1s2, "~/Documents/Upenn/Practicum/2025/Chinatown-Practicum-my/finalresults/property_s1_s2.json", driver = "GeoJSON", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

```{r}
S0_S1_density <- ggplot() +
  
  # Scenario 0: true adjusted sale price
  geom_density(data = property_S1_perc_change %>% filter(adj_sale_price > 100),
               aes(x = adj_sale_price),
               fill = "#eb5600", alpha = 0.6, color = "transparent") +
  
  # Scenario 1: predicted price
  geom_density(data = property_S1_perc_change,
               aes(x = predicted_price),
               fill = "#1a9988", alpha = 0.6, color = "transparent") +

  # median lines
  geom_vline(data = property_S1_perc_change %>% filter(adj_sale_price > 100),
             aes(xintercept = median(adj_sale_price, na.rm = TRUE)),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#eb5600") +
  
  geom_vline(data = property_S1_perc_change,
             aes(xintercept = median(predicted_price, na.rm = TRUE)),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "#1a9988") +

  # log-scale x-axis
  scale_x_log10(labels = dollar) +
  
  # title with markdown color
  labs(
    x = "Price",
    y = "Density",
    title = glue::glue("<span style='color:#eb5600;'>Scenario 0</span> vs. <span style='color:#1a9988;'>Scenario 1</span>")
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_markdown(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# 保存图片
ggsave(
  filename = "~/Documents/Upenn/Practicum/2025/Chinatown-Practicum-my/finalresults/S0_S1_median_density.png",
  plot = S0_S1_density,
  height = 5,
  width = 8.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```
